page: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-100s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring an AMD EPYC processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It delivers 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supported by 32 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16, and cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled with a 100 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this instance.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranks in the top tier, and the Geekbench single-core score is strong. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also perform in the top 25 percent. However, multi-core and parallelized workloads show limitations due to the 2-vCPU hardware constraint; the Geekbench multi-core score, software compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks fall into the bottom 25 percent. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average, but cached small-block read bandwidth is weak.

This server offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The high memory density per core makes it suitable for lightweight databases, text processing, and single-threaded application servers. However, it is less optimal for high-throughput static web serving, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or complex LLM inference, where its performance falls into the lower percentiles.
description: The Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-100s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance powered by a 2.0 GHz AMD EPYC processor with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM. It features a 100 GB NVMe SSD and lacks GPU acceleration. Architecturally, it supports AVX-512 and SHA_NI instructions. Benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core CPU performance and strong single-threaded compression speeds, though multi-core execution, software compilation, and database operations fall into the lower percentiles. With a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, this instance provides a qualitatively cost-effective option for memory-bound, single-threaded tasks. It is best suited for text processing, lightweight database hosting, and single-threaded application workloads, while being less suited for high-throughput web serving or parallelized compute tasks.
